finding.claim: Request body is buffered in an unbounded queue for chunked uploads (no Content-Length); MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH is only enforced after the full body has been received, and never during streaming iteration, enabling memory exhaustion DoS.
finding.source: Client sends a request body with Transfer-Encoding: chunked (no Content-Length header), streaming gigabytes of data.
finding.sink: asyncio.Queue inside Body (request.py:110-111 Body.put), which holds every chunk until the body completes.

trace.note: receive loop reads each http.request message
calls request.body.put(chunk) with no size check
Content-Length precheck only; expected_content_length is None when header absent so nothing is rejected
size check only runs in __await__ after set_complete, once the whole body is in memory
__anext__ streaming iteration performs no MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH check at all

finding.guards_checked: Content-Length precheck (request.py:65-70) bypassed by omitting the header; post-buffer limit (request.py:102-106) runs only after full receipt; BODY_TIMEOUT (request.py:359) covers only form parsing, not get_data() or streaming reads; MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH default 16MB (app.py:230) applies only at the post-buffer check. Whether the ASGI server enforces its own body cap is outside this repo and was not verified.

finding.claim: MultipartDecoder is constructed with self.max_content_length (16MB) as its max_form_memory_size argument instead of self.max_form_memory_size (500KB), so Werkzeug's internal header/boundary buffer can grow to 16MB per request instead of 500KB.
finding.source: Attacker sends a multipart/form-data POST whose part headers never terminate (no CRLFCRLF), so the decoder keeps buffering.
finding.sink: Werkzeug MultipartDecoder internal self.buffer (werkzeug/sansio/multipart.py:139-147 receive_data), capped by the mis-passed argument.

trace.note: passes self.max_content_length as second positional arg (max_form_memory_size slot)
overall body cap of 16MB is the only effective bound on this buffer
Quart's own max_form_memory_size check only counts Data events, not the decoder's header buffer, so it does not cover this path

finding.guards_checked: Overall body cap 16MB (request.py:103); BODY_TIMEOUT 60s (request.py:359) bounds duration. Neither restores the intended 500KB ceiling. Signature verified against Werkzeug at /opt/homebrew/lib/python3.11/site-packages/werkzeug/sansio/multipart.py:84-93,136-147; other Werkzeug versions may differ.

finding.claim: MAX_FORM_PARTS and MAX_FORM_MEMORY_SIZE are not applied to urlencoded form bodies; parse_qsl builds an unbounded number of pairs up to the 16MB body cap, causing CPU and memory amplification.
finding.source: Attacker sends an application/x-www-form-urlencoded POST body of up to 16MB containing millions of key=value pairs.
finding.sink: parse_qsl(...) followed by self.cls(form) at formparser.py:115-119, producing one tuple per pair.

trace.note: _parse_urlencoded calls parse_qsl on the decoded body with no pair-count cap
max_form_parts is only passed to the multipart parser
MAX_FORM_PARTS=1000 config is silently ignored for urlencoded bodies

finding.guards_checked: MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH 16MB via await body (request.py:102-106) and BODY_TIMEOUT (request.py:359). Neither caps the number of pairs, so a 16MB body of 'a=1&' repeated yields roughly 4 million tuples.
